correctness.rationale: Every idempotent coordinate solves a common quadratic aX²−X+bS=0, yielding at most two distinct coordinate values. For nonconstant vectors, u+v=1/a and ratio t=u/v solves k t²−r t+(n−k)=0; t=0,−1 excluded under hypotheses. Each nonconstant idempotent is represented exactly twice by complementary subsets. Repeated roots occur only on discriminant strata and t=1 is excluded at r=n, providing exact case counts and minima from binomial layer inequalities. Independently enumerated all quadratic roots and checked defining equations for n=3,4,5 across generic, symmetry and discriminant values. Numeric sample checks do not replace complex-variable algebraic proof.
